reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of this work lies in replacing outcome-based ratings (Elo, Glicko, TrueSkill) with behavioral signal ranking functions derived from player history. The primary operator Φ sorts players according to weighted behavioral features β, producing a rank list that outperforms traditional systems in terms of NDCG. This approach assumes behavioral consistency and stability, allowing for accurate forecasting even with limited data. The normalized performance ratio (β3–β9) aggregates key behavioral traits into interpretable metrics such as kill-to-damage ratio and survival duration. These ratios are shown to dominate traditional systems especially in sparse-data regimes. The validation method ensures temporal integrity by predicting outcomes chronologically, preventing data leakage. The failure mode occurs when behavioral patterns shift rapidly or when new players lack sufficient historical data to inform reliable rankings.
